summary: Deschutes County, OR summit L-4 ground cab built 1931-32 on Paulina Peak, removed 1968 or 1969; the summit is now a visitor parking area with an overlook.

facts.status_note: Lookout cab removed in 1968 per the register and firelookout.com (1969 per Forest Lookouts); the Oregon Hikers guide describes a summit parking area and overlook today

access.note: Parking area just below the summit, with restrooms and interpretive signs at the overlook; cars are not allowed to drive to the summit in summer, and a shuttle runs from the visitor center

visit.trail_note: Hike from Paulina Lake; the summit area can also be driven to in spring and fall

events.note: Chas. McNeff took over the lookout from G.T. Parker in September 1914 (Bend Bulletin item quoted on Forest Lookouts)
A 12x18-foot cabin erected on the summit during summer 1915 (Forest Lookouts); the register dates the cabin it succeeded to 1917
Cora Leland installed as lookout; a July 1918 newspaper item quoted on Forest Lookouts called her the first woman lookout in Oregon
Virginia Barry took up the post (Ontario Argus item quoted on Forest Lookouts)
L-4 cab built, per the register and firelookout.com; Forest Lookouts dates the L-4 hip-roof ground cabin to 1931
Sylvia Andrews listed as lookout for 1952 and 1953
Sylvia Andrews reported as lookout in August 1954 (Bend Bulletin item quoted on Forest Lookouts)
A new R-6 flat-roof lookout cab constructed on a short tower; no source says what it replaced
L-4 cab removed (register) or destroyed (firelookout.com) in 1968; the Oregon Hikers guide also gives 1917 to 1968
Forest Lookouts records a recommendation to declare the structure surplus and sell it for removal; the Oregon Hikers guide gives 1914 to 1969

corrections.why: 121.9 m is 400 feet. None of the sources read gives a tower height for Paulina Peak. The register and firelookout.com describe a ground cab, and Forest Lookouts gives a short tower only for the 1964 cab.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the cabin the L-4 cab replaced to 1917. Firelookout.com says 1915, and Forest Lookouts describes a 12x18-foot cabin erected in summer 1915. The sources do not reconcile these.
The register and firelookout.com say 1932. Forest Lookouts says 1931 and describes a 14x14-foot hip-roof ground cabin. The sources do not reconcile these.

The register and firelookout.com say 1968, and the guide gives 1917 to 1968 in one passage. Forest Lookouts records a 1969 recommendation to sell the structure for removal, and the guide gives 1914 to 1969 in another passage. No source describes the removal date itself.

notes_for_editor: The brief's height_m of 121.9 m (400 ft) is not supported by any source read and is recorded as a correction. The brief's 'L-4' design and 'ground' kind hold, with the caveat that Forest Lookouts describes a 1964 cab on a short tower. The Oregon Hikers guide is the only source for the site today; it describes a parking area and overlook, but does not say whether any lookout remains are visible. Predecessor, build and removal dates disagree across sources and are shown as conflicts. Cora Leland's 1918 claim appears in two 1918 items on Forest Lookouts with slightly different wording; the story uses the July 18 version. No fires found in the sources read.
